profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary: Developer at Google working on Chat

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
I work on Chat for Android currently.

I've run a few small teams for various projects. I was the lead Android dev for a Meet integration in Chat. This involved a lot of coordination between 6 different teams between all of the different platforms and the frontend and backend of each. I've also been helping out on various performance initiatives for Chat. Before that I worked on Gmail, helping improve the networking layer that's used across gmail, chat, and meet in the Hub (gmail) app. Most of my work has been done in Kotlin, though a decent amount also focuses on Java.
positions.insights: Skills: Java · Software Design · Kotlin · Android Jetpack · Performance Tuning

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I created the Android Profile Video Feature. I then worked on cameras and helped build the rendering system that's used on all of the camera's on android apps (Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, Portal.. etc) which allows for rich effects to be applied onto the camera and existing media. This basically supplies frames for the AR Engine on Android. I also built some minor effects as a proof of concept there.

I then moved onto doing work on Android, Server, and iOS in the messenger assistant team. I worked on voice to text on android and iOS before helping with an SDK migration.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer
positions.description:
I previously did work on infrastructure code for the client-side of the LinkedIn Android flagship application. In my spare time I'm worked SimpleNoSQL (https://github.com/Jearil/SimpleNoSQL) for Android data storage.

I worked on an unreleased services related to employee interactions with each other.

I developed jobs in Pig running on a Hadoop cluster to collate data from multiple sources of our data warehouse and push them to Voldemort (A NoSQL Store). The data was then processed in batch jobs using Scala and Java. Data is collated from multiple internal services before being presented to the user.

I spent time refactoring and and developing an architecture for creating custom communications based on a set of business requirements, data availability, and user preferences.

I worked on increasing our test coverage and testing practices to build a more solid application. My favorite quote from a fellow team member after having pushed unit testing as being a requirement during the code review process was "Hmm, I just found a bug. I guess unit tests really work."

Developed internal tools for monitoring health of deployed services in order to smooth out rapid deployment of the site.

I worked on integrating an acquired product into the LinkedIn ecosystem to improve your contact lists on LinkedIn. Development work is spread across multiple projects in Java, Python, and Hadoop.

positions.title: Senior Technical Yahoo
positions.description: Maintained and updated a custom test case/test plan repository. The system is used to track all of Yahoo's QA test cases and the results from each test. I rewrote the backend of the reporting system, reducing the amount of code to 1/4th of the original size, decoupled the memory requirements from the size of the report, and cut average response time in half. I worked to produce a best practices document and implemented testing on both new and legacy projects. My team role is to research new technologies and seek solutions to new problems that come to our team. My main current tools are: Java, C/C++, Perl, Javascript, HTML/CSS, Maven, Spring, MySQL, memcached, TestNG, Hudson, Git/Subversion, Hadoop/Pig and miscellaneous others.

positions.title: IT Specialist 3 (Programming)
positions.description: Maintained and extended programs for the New York State Archives. Before I came on board they were not using version control for their projects. I set up a subversion repository for the NYS Archives, added tests to existing projects, and implemented continuous integration via cruise control. I also set up and administrated the J2EE server running BEA Weblogic and MySQL on Solaris. My main project was a digital archives project that stored and displayed photographs and maps from the archives. I also worked on constructing a digital repository for archival information about NYS artifacts. The main tools I used were: Java, Bash scripts, Perl, Weblogic, Subversion, Cruise Control, Javascript, HTML/CSS, Hibernate, Spring, MySQL, and PHP.

positions.title: Network and phone administrator and system’s analyst
positions.description: Utech creates medical imaging and reporting software for hospital edoscopy units. When the company relocated in 2005, I set up and administered an asterisk-based VoIP system that served the companies telecommunications needs. I also set up and maintained the companies network infrastructure. I was responsible for implementing new server and network architecture for the company’s home office. Prior to 2005, I worked as a customer support specialist that dealt with over the phone and on-site customer support for Utech’s products.

positions.title: Lead Programmer
positions.description: Laughing Pan Productions produces role-playing and card/strategy games. I took on a volunteer role to work on their community site. The team was distributed throughout the US. Meetings took place over IRC and IM. I worked on a project to implement the mechanical rules of the game for online play. This involved card generators and a backend system for storing result data of each conflict resolution. I also created a web application that was used to facilitate internal communication and weekly status reports. Statistical data of user usage of the tools was kept and used to generate usage reports. My primary tools were: Java, PHP, MySQL, Javascript, IRC, and CVS

patents.title: Architecture for augmenting video data obtained by a client device with one or more effects during rendering
patents.description: A video effects application executes on a client device having an image capture device and receives video data captured by the image capture device. The video effects application extracts information from the captured video data and stores the extracted information as metadata associated with the captured video data. For example, the video effects application identifies objects in the captured video data or identifies optical flow of the captured video data and stores the identified objects or identified optical flow as metadata associated with the captured video data. The video effects application stores information describing modifications to the captured video data in association with the captured video data. When the captured video data is presented, the captured video data, associated metadata, and information describing the modifications is communicated to a renderer, which uses the metadata to perform the identified modifications to the captured video data when presenting the captured video data.

patents.title: Dynamic control of media effects based on hardware performance
patents.description: A media effects engine on a computer device applies one or more effects to an input media stream. A performance monitor monitors a performance metric associated with playing the input media stream and reduces a quality parameter associated with the effect upon detecting a drop in the performance metric below a target metric. The quality parameter manages a tradeoff between a quality of effect and an amount of hardware resources consumed to produce the effect. Thus, the effect can be adjusted to meet the capabilities of the computer device.
